questions_and_answers.question_text: What is the literal meaning of míngbai?
What are the two senses of míngbai?
What does tīngmíngbai mean — and what does it NOT mean?
Name the three meanings of tímù.
Write the Chinese for "Now I see."
Write the Chinese for "I couldn't understand a thing in yesterday's class."

answers.answer_text: Zuótiānde kè wǒ yìdiǎnr dōu tīngbumíngbai.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Which other perception verb can take míngbai as its result?
Write the Chinese for "This matter is very clear."

answers.answer_text: "Way of saying a thing; statement, version, argument."

articles.text:
2. A: Tāde shuōfǎ wǒ méi tīngdǒng,  I didn't understand the way he said
      nǐ tīngmíngbai le ma?          that. Did you understand it?
   B: Méiyou, wǒ yě méi tīngmíngbai, No, I didn't understand it either.
      érqiě zhèige tímù yě tài nán   Moreover, this topic is too hard.
      le.

Notes on No. 2

míngbai: "to be clear on, to understand," literally, "bright-white." This is an adjectival verb which MAY OR MAY NOT be followed by an object.

Xiànzài wǒ míngbai le.           Now I see.
Wǒ míngbai nǐde yìsi.            I understand what you mean.

Míngbai can also mean "to be clear, to be obvious":

Zhèijiàn shìqing hěn míngbai.    This matter is very clear/obvious.

tīngmíngbai: "to hear and understand." This is a compound verb of result with an ADJECTIVAL VERB indicating the result. But note carefully: tīngmíngbai means ONLY "to understand by listening," NOT "to hear clearly." Use tīngqīngchu to mean "to hear clearly."

Zuótiānde kè wǒ yìdiǎnr dōu      I couldn't understand a thing in
tīngbumíngbai.                   yesterday's class.
Gāngcái lǎoshī shuōde wǒ méi     I didn't hear (clearly) what the
tīngqīngchu.                     teacher just said.

Another verb of perception which can take míngbai is kàn, "to see, to read":

Nǐ kàn méi kànmíngbai zhèige     Did you understand the question (when
tímù?                            you read it)?

tímù: This noun has THREE commonly used meanings: (1) "topic, subject," (2) "title," and (3) "question, problem" (e.g., on a test).

Wǒmen jīntian huàn yíge tán      Today let's change the topic of
huàde tímù.                      conversation.
Zhèiběn shūde tímù shi           The title of this book is Chinese
Zhōngguóde Shèhuì.               Society.
Zuótiān kǎoshìde tímù nàme duō.  There were so many problems on
                                 yesterday's test.
